title: Invention of the Mondaloy superalloy
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Invention of the Mondaloy superalloy, about 1990s-2012 at Rockwell Science Center; Air Force Research Laboratory, Wright-Patterson AFB, and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.
place_text: Rockwell Science Center; Air Force Research Laboratory, Wright-Patterson AFB

tellings.quote: The stalemate finally shattered in the 1990s thanks to the hard work of Dallas Hardwick and Monica Resza at the Rockwell Science Center.

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the 1990s two researchers, Dallas Hardwick and Monica Resza at the Rockwell Science Center, a corporate research lab, broke a long deadlock and created Mondaloy, a superalloy, meaning a metal blend built to survive extreme heat and stress. He points to a report from the National Academies, the US scientific advisory body, and to the Mondaloy patents, and connects the work to the Air Force Research Laboratory at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio. He tells it in an episode about top American scientists going missing.
